method: For this weeks homework, I was asked to read an academic article about war and technology and a section from a book about the intersection between art and technology, and was also asked to write up about the connection between art and technology in relation to 2 things, A Bicycle Built for Two Thousand and a clip from 2001: A Space Odyssey. related_work: For our first week's lecture, we analysed 2 paintings from the 1930s, both named Hollywood, by Thomas Hart Benton. I said for both these paintings that there was 'a juxtaposition between cinema and war, between fictionalised drama and real world destruction.' We were also introduced to Impressionism and the work of Jackson Pollock.
results_discussion:
A Bicycle Built for Two Thousand:
The first thing the listener can notice is the way in which all the voices come together to, one, create a musical Choir that is not quite in pitch, whose mish mash of human humming creates something in which the human voice is distorted greatly to the extent that almost none of the words that the humans actually say is audible, yet also sounds human. The computer with their electronic synthesisers produces a sound that sounds in pitch, but that also sounds completely like something made by a computer, from the computerised notes to the robotic singing, the difference is a song that is much more easily decipherable and listenable, but that lacks the human component. In conclusion, this is a piece that combines musical performance and technology in a bizarrely intriguing way, showing the usage of human labour and technology to produce a unique and creative piece of musical art.
2001: A Space Odyssey:
This clip from 2001 provides a perfect example of a computer that has been programmed to sound like it has been humanised, and the agency that Hal tries to use to prevent it from being turned off. There’s a slow burning tension in the time that it takes for Dave to travel to Hal’s nervous centre and start removing the things that give him life, including the use of sound or the lack thereof. During this time Hal tries to plead with Dave to keep his life, trying to conceit but failing to convince Dave to turn around and change his mind. The ending of the clip, where Hal loses its memory, its voice, and then recites the original song it was taught with near the end of its life, ultimately shows the emotional agency that Hal tries to portray to Dave, as a computer and an Artificial Intelligence system.
title: A Bicycle Built for Two Thousand and 2001
introduction: This week was my first lesson in Ideas in Art and Technology. I was introduced to the lecturer, Ryan, who stated that "There's no such thing as art without technology." I was introduced to the lesson structure and the means of assessment, weekly text based writing assignments. He said that the module would be a "lot of fun" but that it'd be a lot in a short period of time. He also said there'd be a lot of reading which made of a better artist.
